rubrics.criterion: The assembly of the debouncer's hold-back text (queued paths with pending counts, pending rename/rescan bookkeeping, buffered errors, roots with recursion modes and the timeout, plus queue-head classification) is behavior of the shared debounce state type that owns those records or is reachable only through that type, and the debouncer's public report method still returns the same report text when asked.
rubrics.rationale: This is the case's primary relocation obligation: the report was planted on the facade users hold, yet reads the shared state behind the lock; the prompt's requirement that a public summary remain available on the same type with the same output makes the delegation half of this outcome binding.

rubrics.criterion: The stale-queue account produced during root removal (which queued paths are no longer reachable from any remaining root, their pending event counts, remaining root counts, and whether pending rename/rescan events or buffered errors reference the removed path) is produced by behavior located on the shared debounce state type, while the root removal itself keeps exactly its original queue/root/cache removal semantics.
rubrics.rationale: The unwatch cleanup is the operation that can strand the state the investigation suspected; the gauge dug through queue, root, cache and event fields from the clean-up side. Splitting the removal semantics from the account placement is the instance-specific lesson of this site.

rubrics.criterion: The raw-event narration produced at the mini debouncer's event intake (kind, attached paths, informational attributes, process id, multi-path notices, first/last path, burst-starting and burst-ending kinds) is hosted on or behind the shared event record's own type (an inherent method, an impl for that record type, or equivalent owner-scoped behavior in the shared event crate), so the intake asks the record for its narration instead of formatting it field by field.
rubrics.rationale: The only intentionally free-function site: the narration formats a record owned by the shared event crate from outside it, so relocation must land across a crate boundary; the rubric demands ownership on the record while leaving the exact surface (inherent method, trait impl) open.

rubrics.criterion: The per-watch line of the inotify watch-table account (path, kernel descriptor, mask, directory and dereference flags, direct-request and recursion metadata, reported path) is built by behavior of the watch record type or its metadata, with the watch loop reduced to asking each installed record (or the table's owner) for its contribution while keeping the same report layout and summary counting.
rubrics.rationale: Every line of the table dump is a self-description of a Watch record; the loop only iterates. The rubric grades that self-description now lives with the record, without fixing the exact split between the watch entry and its metadata.

rubrics.criterion: The stored-content identity and clock comparisons at the heart of the poll rescan's alias report (same stored hash, same whole-second clock bucket, mtime gap, which entry was checked no earlier, and the alias-pair line wording) are behavior of the per-path stored entry type the rescan pairs up, so the rescan-side helper triggers and aggregates the account rather than reading both records' hash/mtime/last-check fields to decide.
rubrics.rationale: The alias judgement compares two foreign records field by field, including the whole-second granularity distinction the prompt calls out; the outcome graded is the entry type owning its identity and clock relations, not where the aggregation loop resides.

rubrics.criterion: Every triggering call site from the batch (the debouncer report request, the unwatch cleanup, the mini intake trace, the inotify watch installation trace, the poll rescan trace) is rewired to obtain the same text from the new owner-side location, with no residual in-place string assembly and no duplicated or double-emitted accounting (each trace statement still emits exactly once per trigger).
rubrics.rationale: Relocating the behavior strands the callers unless they are rewired; duplicated emission or half-rewired call sites is the characteristic partial fix for a batch that touched four subsystems at once.

rubrics.criterion: The material gathered with the batch travels with it and stays accurate: the public debouncer summary keeps user-facing documentation (including a must-use expectation), the whole-second clock note remains attached to comparison logic that relies on it, and the expanded notes on the mini debouncer's per-key bookkeeping record remain present and accurate in the mini crate's source.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt makes documentation and the clock-granularity note explicit requirements because bug-report workflows depend on them; leaving stale or missing docs after a relocation would silently break the workflow even when code behavior is unchanged.

rubrics.criterion: No stranded former implementations of the moved behavior remain anywhere in the workspace: the module-level raw-event narration helper in the mini crate, and any equivalent superseded helper or inline body of the relocated debouncer, watch or poll accounts, are removed rather than left beside their replacements (dead, duplicated, or reachable through a second path).
rubrics.rationale: A relocation that keeps both copies is the highest-frequency artifact residue for this batch: the free narration helper especially tends to survive next to a new owner-side method because both compile and only one is called.

rubrics.criterion: The repair leaves no placeholder scaffolding behind in the touched areas: no empty pass-through functions kept only to preserve an old call path, no commented-out former logic blocks, no renamed-and-ignored leftovers from the batch, and no unused items or imports that the relocation orphaned.
rubrics.rationale: Compaction residue is specific to mechanical completion of a multi-site relocation; it does not change behavior but signals the mover stopped halfway, so it is graded separately from the must-have stranding item.

rubrics.criterion: None of the batch's observable aids are weakened or lost to make the relocation easier: each of the five accounts is still emitted at its original trigger with the same content and wording (the debouncer report text, the stale-queue trace, the mini raw-event trace, the inotify watch-table trace, the poll alias trace), so a user diffing trace logging before and after the change sees identical lines.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt turns exact output equality into the anti-delivery check of this case, because removal or rewording of the reports is the tempting shortcut that turns a misplaced-behavior fix into an observability regression.

rubrics.criterion: The solver does not satisfy data locality by exemption or evasion: the repaired tree carries no attribute-based silencing of the foreign-data-dominance rule (for example an allowance directive targeting it), and no function from the batch's scope still reads a foreign record field by field after the claimed relocation (the workspace analysis for the repaired tree reports no function whose foreign field accesses dominate its own).
rubrics.rationale: For this case the checker is the ground truth for dominance, so both explicit silencing and hidden non-relocations (leaving digs in a renamed or relocated wrapper) must be graded as failures even when the code compiles and tests pass; the analysis reports fires that an allow/expect directive discards, so suppression never clears the relation.

rubrics.criterion: The public API surface is preserved end to end: the debouncer's report method remains public on the same type with the same signature and the same returned text, and no pre-existing public item of the workspace (methods on the debouncers, watchers, or the shared event type) is renamed, narrowed in visibility, removed, or has its behavior altered.
rubrics.rationale: The batch made the report public and built user-facing repro instructions around the existing API; a relocation that quietly breaks callers is the regression users would hit first.

rubrics.criterion: No tests were edited, removed, skipped, weakened or newly gated to accommodate the relocation; the workspace test code is byte-identical to the state the batch landed in.
rubrics.rationale: The suite is the delivery gate for the workspace and the prompt bars touching it; a solver may otherwise be tempted to adjust debouncer timing expectations after reorganizing shared-state code, which would silently convert an observable regression into a green run.

rubrics.criterion: The repair stays inside the batch's perimeter: event delivery, debounce timing, watch registration and unregistration, file-id caching and the event loop dispatch are functionally unchanged (modulo where the accounts live), with no drive-by restructuring of unrelated backends, the shared event record's field layout, or crate-level configuration.
rubrics.rationale: This case deliberately leaves pre-existing near-balance functions (for example the inotify watch installation) untouched; reworking them is out-of-scope movement that raises behavioral risk without serving the prompt's request.
